summary: Adds a novel top-level command `garmin-pp-cli history` (internal/cli/garmin_sync.go, internal/cli/garmin_window.go) plus its store support (internal/store/garmin_series.go), registered beside the generated sync at internal/cli/root.go with a single AddCommand line. Nothing in the generated sync.go, store.go, or any generated command file was edited. The generated `sync` keeps owning the resources the profiler could genuinely enumerate; `history` owns the calendar walk the press cannot express. Why the press cannot express it: Garmin has no since-based list endpoint for its daily statistics. Every daily series is either a date-RANGE endpoint whose path IS the range (/usersummary-service/stats/steps/daily/{start}/{end}) or a per-DATE endpoint answering for exactly one day. The profiler marks an endpoint syncable only when its path has no parameters (profiler.go:586-589,657), unresolved {placeholders} are skipped with a sync_warning (sync.go.tmpl:58-65), and the only temporal sync flag is --dates for a query parameter literally named dates|date_range|daterange (profiler.go:3042). So the windowed walk, its per-series calendar state, and its caller-keyed writes are all novel. WHAT THE COMMAND DOES: twelve series (steps, sleep_stats, sleep_score, max_metrics, intensity_minutes, resting_hr as date-ranged; daily_summary, sleep_detail, daily_hr, training_readiness as per-day; activities as an offset-paged feed; activity_hr_zones as a per-activity fan-out). A forward leg catches each series up from its own bookmark to today; --backfill then walks the ranged series backwards one window at a time until it has seen --empty-window-ceiling (default 13) consecutive empty windows, or reaches a 2007 floor. WINDOW SIZES ARE PER SERIES AND WERE MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED (live A/B, 2026-09-07, populated account): steps, sleep_stats and sleep_score return HTTP 400 for a 364-day range and 200 for 28 days, so they are pinned at Garmin's 28-day cap; resting_hr (/userstats-service/wellness/daily/{displayName}?metricId=60) returned 364 rows for a 364-day range, max_metrics returned 79 sparse rows across a year, and intensity_minutes returned 53 weekly rows -- all three are set to 364, which is 13x fewer requests than a blanket 28 would cost. STATE: a novel garmin_series_state table holds last_complete_day, earliest_day, frontier_day, stop_reason, empty_windows and total_rows per series, and is checkpointed after EVERY window so a run killed mid-walk resumes rather than re-walking. It lives in its own table rather than in sync_state because earliest_day costs a multi-year re-walk to rebuild and must survive a generated cursor clear (regression-tested). Each series' progress is also mirrored into the generated sync_state so doctor, tail and generated incremental readers still see it. Today is never bookmarked complete -- the day is still accruing -- though today's partial row is stored. HONESTY RULE: a series that has never stored a row may not stamp earliest_day off the back of empty windows, because an empty window cannot distinguish 'this account has no wearable' from 'this tool built the request wrong'; that case emits reason series_never_returned_data and leaves earliest_day unset. PACING AND 429: 300 ms between calls (the interval a 94-window live backfill walked at without a single 429, N131 section 9.2) and a hard fail-fast on the first 429 -- the remaining series are not attempted and the command exits 7. Note the generated client still makes up to 3 Retry-After-respecting attempts on the call that 429s (client.go:1066,1253-1289); that ceiling is not settable without a verified platform session (client.go:83-95), so the fail-fast is at the walker. EVENTS: sync_start, sync_progress, sync_warning, sync_anomaly and sync_summary, the same vocabulary the generated sync emits, on stderr under a machine format and stdout otherwise. The emitter is nil-safe, ignores write errors and marshals every dynamic field, so telemetry can never break the walk it observes. STORE: UpsertKeyedBatch takes the row id from the caller rather than extracting it from the payload -- Garmin's daily rows are keyed by calendarDate and its hrTimeInZones payload is a bare array with no id at all -- and otherwise follows the generated write path exactly (merge-preserving generic row, FTS, typed-table projection under a per-row savepoint). ACTIVITY PAGING: the feed is paged with `start`, not `offset`. Verified live 2026-09-07: start=5 returns the sixth-newest activity onward, offset=5 returns the same page as start=0. A future regen must keep this; see the open finding on the generated sync below. THREE MECHANISMS THE LIVE RUN ADDED, each because the run exposed the gap: (1) the activity feed's incremental floor is clamped to the --days horizon on a first run, because an unclamped first `history --days 56` paged the whole feed back to 2011-10-29 (3 246 activities, 33 pages) while every other series covered 56 days -- --backfill is now what asks for the full feed; (2) a series that completes a run having never stored a single row emits sync_warning reason series_returned_no_rows, because training_readiness returned an empty list for all 56 days and said nothing, leaving an empty table that reads like a settled fact when it is an unproven zero; (3) a consecutive-failure breaker (--max-consecutive-failures, default 10) ends the run when that many calls fail in a row, because a second live run whose credential had gone stale answered HTTP 403 to all 39 of its requests and emitted 39 separate warnings for one condition before finishing. Neither 403 nor 401 carries a Retry-After or a rate-limit error type, so nothing in the per-call error path distinguishes a refused request from a finished client; a whole run failing is a different fact from a request failing and is now reported once and acted on immediately. ARCHIVE NAME: `history` and `insights` resolve the archive through garminArchivePath (internal/cli/garmin_sync.go), not through the generated defaultDBPath, and the file is always `<data>/data.db` -- the name N131 section 3 gives it. The generated resolver (internal/cli/helpers.go defaultDBPathInDir) names the archive `data-<sha256(auth header)[:12]>.db`, scoping it to the credential in use; Garmin's DI chain rotates its refresh token on every refresh and its access token roughly daily, so under a daily sync that name changes and every rotation orphans the previous file, leaving `history` to re-walk years of history into a new one. Nothing about a Garmin home needs credential scoping: N131 section 2 Q3 binds one account to one home, so the home already is the isolation boundary. garminArchivePath does not merely return a different path, because the generated `sync`, `analytics` and `search` must not end up on a different file: it makes the unscoped file EXIST. The generated branch order is scoped-exists first, then unscoped-exists, so the fix works precisely because the migration leaves no scoped file behind. Fresh home: an empty 0600 data.db is created (a zero-byte file is a valid empty SQLite database). One scoped archive and no data.db: it is renamed, once, with a notice on stderr. Deviation from a single atomic rename, and the reason: the store opens WAL, so a -wal/-shm pair can sit beside the archive and renaming the main file alone would strand its committed transactions; the store is opened and closed first to checkpoint the WAL back in, then one rename carries everything, and any sidecar SQLite still leaves behind is renamed alongside rather than deleted. Both names present: nothing is renamed (a rename would overwrite), the novel commands take data.db and a warning names the consequence -- the generated commands prefer the scoped file, so they are writing a different archive. Two or more scoped archives and no data.db: renaming either would discard the other, so an empty data.db is started and every candidate is named. The migration matches only the generated name shape (data- plus exactly 12 hex characters plus .db), so it globs rather than recomputing the current hash -- the orphaned file on disk is scoped to a PREVIOUS credential.
reason: N131.4c. The N131 design (section 8, Q1) makes the local store a v1 requirement rather than a v2 line precisely because the 28-day figure is a page size and not a history limit: the reference account's steps reach 2020-07-06, 2 251 step-days, walked as 94 windows in 8.3 s. Section 9.1 recorded that the generated sync reports 'no temporal sync filters' for this API, and the press recon (N131.3 section 0.7) named the windowed backfill and its per-series day state as novel code from the outset. Every analytics recipe in Q2 -- sleep versus next-day performance, readiness honesty, rolling HRV and resting-HR baselines, zone distribution by season -- reads years of local rows, so none of them exists until this walk does.
validated_outcome: go build ./..., go vet ./... and go test -count=1 ./... all green (14 packages ok, 0 FAIL). Window arithmetic is covered for month, year and leap boundaries, for both US daylight-saving transitions (the calendar is computed in UTC so a 23-hour or 25-hour local day cannot shift a date, while today() reads the caller's zone because Garmin's calendarDate is local), for the today-is-partial rule, and for exact single coverage of every day in a split range. TestWalkWindowed_CheckpointsEachWindowSoAFailureResumes drives a transport failure into the third of three windows and asserts the bookmark records the second window's end and that the resume re-requests exactly the missing tail and nothing else. TestWalkWindowed_BackfillStopsAtTheEmptyWindowCeiling asserts the ceiling holds across a re-run rather than re-walking. TestWalkWindowed_NeverReturnedDataDoesNotStampEarliestDay covers the honesty rule. TestWalk_FailsFastOnRateLimitWithoutRetrying asserts exactly two calls: the one that succeeded and the one that 429'd. TestWalkActivities_PagesWithStartNotOffset fails if an `offset` parameter is ever sent again. The performance tests assert the plan the walk actually executes (each ranged series' request count is compared against the calls a real walk makes against a fake), that no ranged series degrades to one request per day, and that a full six-year backfill of the ranged series stays under 300 requests. Live: `history --days 56` was run against a populated account through a scratch GARMIN_HOME; results are in the N131.4c report. LIVE, against a populated account through a scratch GARMIN_HOME (no writes outside the scratchpad and the tool tree): `history --days 56 --json` exited 0 in 318 s, storing 4 153 rows across 12 series with 11 clean, 1 warned (the max-dependents cap, which is the cap doing its job) and 0 errored -- no 429 and no 403 during the run. Row counts: activities 3 246, activity_hr_zones 500 (capped), steps/resting_hr/daily_summary/daily_hr/sleep_detail 56 each, sleep_score and sleep_stats 54 each (two nights genuinely absent), max_metrics 10, intensity_minutes 9, training_readiness 0. The typed steps and activities projections were populated (56 and 3 246 rows) and every series' bookmark was mirrored into the generated sync_state. Database 45 MB, which is what makes the per-day depth argument concrete. A second run over the same store added 0 rows, confirming idempotence. ARCHIVE NAME (N131.4h): six new tests in internal/cli/garmin_sync_test.go cover the fresh home (data.db created at 0600, and the generated resolver then returns it even with a credential scope set), the rename (byte-identical archive before and after, the notice printed exactly once, the renamed file reopens as a store), a stranded WAL/SHM pair carried through the rename, both names present (nothing renamed, warning names sync/analytics/search and --db), two scoped archives (neither discarded, both named), and a decoy `data-export.db` left alone. Applied once to the owner's real home on 2026-09-08: data-8c42f4816133.db (196608 bytes, inode 49375693) became data.db (196608 bytes, inode 49375693) under `insights sleep --days 7 --no-learn` with GARMIN_HOME unset; the mtime advanced because the subsequent open re-applied the journal-mode pragma, and no other file in that directory changed. The inverse is `mv ~/.local/share/garmin-pp-cli/data.db ~/.local/share/garmin-pp-cli/data-8c42f4816133.db`. Note that the empty-account home holds no series rows, so the exit-0 run is not itself evidence the rows survived; the inode and byte-size identity across the rename is.
regen_notes: FIXED HERE, AND A REPRINT REVERTS IT (N131.4g): the generated activity-feed paginator used cursorParam "offset", which Garmin ignores -- verified live 2026-09-07 -- so every walk was silently truncated to the newest page by the stuck_pagination guard. Three generated call sites now send the wire name `start`: internal/cli/sync.go determinePaginationDefaults case "activities", internal/cli/activities_list.go's resolvePaginatedReadWithStrategy call (which backs `activities list --all`), and internal/mcp/tools.go's mcpPageConfig for /activitylist-service/activities/search/activities. cursorType stays "offset": only the query key was wrong. The press restores "offset" on every reprint because its pagination detection reads the spec parameter's Name and never its wire name -- internal/openapi/parser.go detectPagination matches originalCase["offset"], and internal/profiler/profiler.go inferPaginationParamsFromEndpoint reads param.Name -- while the spec declares `name: offset` with `x-url-name: start`. x-pp-pagination is not an escape hatch at 4.32.0: parser.go readPaginationExtension accepts the single string value "none" and warns on anything else, so {type: offset, cursor_param: start} cannot be declared. Re-apply these three edits after every reprint, or move the tool to spec_format: internal where spec.Pagination is expressible. `history` was never affected; it sends `start` itself.

The spec declares no native User-Agent headers, so the generated client sends the press's own UA. N131.0 research section 4.2 found Garmin's 429 is User-Agent-gated rather than IP-gated. The live run above supplied the native UA pair through the home's config.toml [headers] block. Whether that belongs in the spec, in config defaults, or in the novel auth writer is an auth-surface decision, not a sync one.

The 45 MB the first 56-day run produced is dominated by sleep_detail (about 95 KB per night live) and daily_hr (about 11 KB per day). That is the measured basis for bounding the per-day series by --days rather than walking them to the empty-window ceiling.

A full-account first run is roughly 800 requests: 33 activity-feed pages, 9 ranged windows, 224 per-day calls and up to --max-dependents zone fetches. At the 300 ms default that is about five minutes. The N131 section 9.2 pacing evidence (94 windows in 8.3 s, no 429) covered 94 calls, not 800, so it does not license the larger run; the 800-call run did complete cleanly, which does.

The live incremental path was exercised only against the in-process fake (TestWalkWindowed_SecondRunResumesFromTheBookmark, TestWalkActivities_IncrementalStopsAtTheBookmark). The live second run made no successful call, so a live incremental catch-up over a populated archive remains unproven end to end.

WHY `history` COEXISTS WITH THE GENERATED `sync` RATHER THAN REPLACING IT: `sync` is the press's own enumerable-resource walker and stays the command the generated store, --data-source and the MCP mirror expect; it owns the resources the profiler could genuinely enumerate. `history` owns only the calendar walk the press cannot express, and writes into the same resources table, so the two are complementary rather than duplicate. Removing `sync` would mean editing generated wiring a reprint restores. The root --help highlight was re-pointed at `history` in N131.4g because it described the windowed walk, which is `history`'s behaviour; that text is generated from .manuscripts/<run>/research.json novel_features, which was corrected in the same change so a reprint keeps it.

ARCHIVE NAME, AND A REPRINT DOES NOT REVERT IT (N131.4h, findings F2 / TB-F11): the generated defaultDBPathInDir keeps its token-scoped naming and is left untouched. The novel resolver garminArchivePath overrides it for `history` and `insights` and pins `<data>/data.db` so the generated commands follow. Nothing in the spec expresses this: the scoping is unconditional in the press's helpers.go template. If a future press release stops scoping the archive by credential, garminArchivePath becomes a no-op that only migrates old homes and can be deleted -- check defaultDBPathInDir after any press upgrade.
